newsitem.title: CANADA: MOTOR RACING-PANIS BREAKS BOTH LEGS IN CANADIAN CRASH.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-PANIS BREAKS BOTH LEGS IN CANADIAN CRASH.

text.p: Frenchman Olivier Panis broke both his legs when he crashed during Sunday's Canadian Grand Prix, won by Germany's Michael Schumacher in a Ferrari.
An official bulletin issed by the organisers two hours after the race said he had suffered double fractures in each leg when he crashed heavily after 51 laps.
The bulletin said: "After having been transferred to Sacre-Coeur Hospital, further examinations on Olivier Panis have indicated that he sustained double closed fractures to both legs.
"An orthopaedic operation will be performed during the evening."
Panis lost control of his Prost car during the closing stages of the dramatic race when he slithered off the track and into the barrier on a high-speed section of the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve.
His car rebounded twice off the barrier before plunging into a wall of tyres. The front end of the car was severely damaged by the impact.

The race was overshadowed by accidents from the start, with favourite Jacques Villeneuve of Canada crashing on lap two in his Williams after surviving a first corner collision which had eliminated three cars -- Briton Eddie Irvine's Ferrari, Dane Jan Magnussen's Stewart and Finn Mika Hakkinen's McLaren.

Japanese Ukyo Katayama crashed in his Minardi on lap six and German Ralf Schumacher thundered into a tyre wall on lap 14 on a day on which severe tyre-wear undermined the best efforts of all the drivers on the treacherous low-grip circuit.
